title: Linear Sqrt Decibel Scaling Chart
description: One fixed 16-bin power spectrum redrawn under linear, square-root, and decibel scaling, with a dynamic caption naming which bins become invisible.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Spectrum Display
Data Visualization
chapter_title: Computing and Displaying a Real Spectrum

learningObjectives: Compare the same spectrum under three scalings
Judge which scaling reveals quiet content best
prerequisites: A spectrum is magnitude per bin

controls.label: Any bar
controls.purpose: Tooltip with raw power and displayed value

simulationModel.modelType: Display-only rescaling of a fixed spectrum
assumptions: Decibels referenced to the peak bin, floored at -60 dB
limitations: Uses a synthetic spectrum chosen to make the contrast clear; real spectra vary in how starkly the modes differ

keyQuestions: Which bins disappear under linear scaling despite carrying real power?
What does the decibel view understate?
commonMisconceptions: That decibel scaling is universally the right choice
That an invisible bar means no energy at that frequency
assessmentOpportunities: Convert a 1%-of-peak component to dB and judge its visibility
